cards.front: VBG-to-ABG conversion offsets? pH: VBG 0.02–0.04 lower. pCO₂: VBG 3–8 mmHg higher. HCO₃⁻: [___]. Lactate: Same. PaO₂: Cannot assess from VBG.
cards.context:
VBG correlates well for pH, pCO₂, lactate, electrolytes. Main limitation: cannot assess PaO₂.

Use SpO₂ for oxygenation screening; ABG only when precise PaO₂/P:F ratio needed.

cards.front: Tourniquets are safe for up to 2 hours; always document [___] of application.
cards.context:
The 2-hour tourniquet window comes from military trauma data: ischaemic nerve injury and reperfusion complications are rare under 2 hours, increase between 2-6 hours, and become common beyond 6.

The time-of-application written on the tourniquet (or limb) is critical for downstream decisions: short interval = release once volume-resuscitated and bleeding controlled by other.

The bigger error is hesitating to apply one when needed — uncontrolled extremity haemorrhage is rapidly fatal.

cards.front: Earliest sign of opioid toxicity is [___] (before respiratory depression). Titrate naloxone to respiratory rate, not full alertness.
cards.context: Sedation appears before respiratory depression — it's the warning sign to act on. Titrate naloxone gently to restore breathing (not full consciousness) to avoid precipitating acute withdrawal and agitation.

cards.front: ATLS Class II haemorrhagic shock: [___] mL blood loss, HR 100-120, BP normal.
cards.context:
The ATLS classes are deliberately tachycardia-anchored, not BP-anchored.

This is why a trauma patient with normal BP and a heart rate of 110 should be treated as actively bleeding until proven otherwise, with permissive hypotension targets (SBP ~90 in non-TBI), MTP activation if needed.

cards.front: The most common and most frequently missed delirium subtype is [___].
cards.context:
Hypoactive delirium is the most common subtype (~50%) and the most dangerous because it is frequently missed. A quiet, withdrawn patient may be labeled as 'tired' or 'depressed' when they are actually delirious.

Hypoactive delirium carries worse outcomes than hyperactive.

cards.front: Skin/soft tissue sepsis first-line: [___] 2 g IV q6h. If MRSA risk (IVDU, recent hospitalisation, nursing home, known colonisation) → add vancomycin.
cards.context:
Empirical cover for skin/soft tissue sepsis targets MSSA and group A strep, and broadens to include MRSA only when specific risk factors are present.

When MRSA is plausible — IVDU, recent hospitalisation, nursing home residence, or known colonisation — flucloxacillin no longer covers the likely organism, so vancomycin is added (renally dosed.

cards.front: During massive transfusion protocol (MTP), hypocalcaemia from [___] toxicity causes hypotension and prolonged QT. Treat with IV calcium.
cards.context:
Stored blood is anticoagulated with citrate; normal volumes clear within minutes, but in MTP the load outstrips clearance and citrate binds free ionised calcium — sometimes precipitously.

Check iCa (not total — only the ionised fraction is active) every 4-6 units PRBCs in MTP; replace with 10 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV (or CaCl₂ centrally) for symptoms or iCa <1.0 mmol/L.

cards.front: EpiPen Jr (150 mcg) can be used from 7.5 kg; adult 300 mcg device from 20 kg; 500 mcg device from [___] kg.
cards.context: 150 mcg autoinjectors (EpiPen Jr, Anapen Jr) can be used in children over 7.5 kg. This is important for discharge planning and parent education.

cards.front: Inotrope increases myocardial contractility, vasopressor causes vasoconstriction, and chronotrope changes heart [___].
cards.context: Use IVC to decode cardiovascular drug actions quickly under pressure.

cards.front: A-a gradient = [___] minus PaO₂. Age-adjusted upper limit (mmHg) ≈ (age÷4) + 4 mmHg.
cards.context:
A-a gradient quantifies gas exchange efficiency. Normal widens with age.

Elevated A-a = intrinsic lung pathology (V/Q mismatch, shunt, diffusion impairment). Normal A-a with hypoxaemia = hypoventilation (lungs fine).

cards.front: 4% dextrose + 0.18% saline is ideal maintenance because 2.5 L delivers ~[___] mmol Na — matching Holliday-Segar daily requirements.
cards.context: For a 70kg patient, daily needs are ~2500mL water and 75mmol sodium. 4% dextrose + 0.18% saline delivers exactly this — it's physiologically designed maintenance, not resuscitation.

cards.front: CPP = MAP − ICP, target [___] mmHg in TBI.
cards.context:
CPP is the driving pressure for cerebral blood flow. Too low causes secondary brain injury from ischaemia; too high requires excessive vasopressor support which increases pulmonary complications.

Balance is key.

cards.front: The FEAST trial showed fluid boluses in febrile African children [___] 48-hour mortality (RR 1.45).
cards.context:
The FEAST trial is one of the most important and counterintuitive results in resuscitation.

This challenges the automatic assumption that fluid boluses are beneficial in all shock.

cards.front: DOACs should be ceased [___] hours pre-operatively depending on renal clearance.
cards.context: Managing medications perioperatively is a key preoperative assessment skill. Some drugs must continue, others must be withheld.

cards.front: In repeated supratherapeutic ingestion (RSTI) of paracetamol, NAC is not needed if ALT <[___] and paracetamol level <20 mg/L.
cards.context:
The Rumack-Matthew nomogram is for SINGLE acute ingestion; staggered or repeated supratherapeutic ingestion (RSTI) needs different rules.

If ALT is already elevated, hepatotoxicity is in progress regardless of the paracetamol level — start NAC.

cards.front: Target MAP in septic shock is at least [___] mmHg.
cards.context:
MAP ≥65 mmHg is the Surviving Sepsis perfusion target — derived from SEPSISPAM (NEJM 2014) which compared MAP 65-70 to MAP 80-85 and found no mortality difference but more atrial fibrillation in the high-MAP arm.

Individualise upward in patients with chronic hypertension (target MAP 75-85 reduces AKI in this subgroup per SEPSISPAM subgroup) or evidence of poor end-organ perfusion at MAP 65 (oliguria, lactate not clearing.

cards.front: Key damage control resuscitation targets: pH greater than [___], lactate less than 4 mmol/L, ionised calcium greater than 1.1 mmol/L, and temperature greater than 35°C.
cards.context:
Resuscitation targets during damage control provide specific endpoints to guide product replacement. These numbers should be checked every 30-60 minutes during active MTP.

TBI patients have higher targets because the injured brain tolerates coagulopathy and anaemia poorly.

cards.front: Critical pH threshold for severe acidaemia (risk of cardiac arrest)? Below [___]
cards.context: Extreme pH impairs enzyme function, myocardial contractility, and catecholamine responsiveness. Below 7.1 or above 7.6, mortality rises sharply even with treatment of underlying cause.

cards.front: For sustained-release opioid overdose, naloxone infusion rate is approximately [___] of the effective bolus dose per hour.
cards.context:
Naloxone half-life is short (~30-60 min) but most opioids last much longer — methadone (12-36 h), MS Contin / OxyContin (12-24 h), buprenorphine (24-72 h), body-packers' parcels (variable).

Run an infusion at ~⅔ of the effective bolus dose per hour to maintain reversal — a typical regimen is 0.4 mg bolus, then 0.27 mg/h infusion, titrated up if RR drops or down if withdrawal symptoms emerge.

cards.front: In haemostatic resuscitation, permissive hypotension targets a systolic BP of [___] mmHg until surgical control.
cards.context:
Targeting normal blood pressure in active haemorrhage increases bleeding by disrupting early clot formation ('popping the clot').

Exception: do NOT use permissive hypotension in TBI — the injured brain needs perfusion pressure.

cards.front: A-a gradient = PAO₂ minus PaO₂. Age-adjusted upper limit (mmHg) ≈ (age÷4) + [___].
cards.context:
A-a gradient quantifies gas exchange efficiency. Normal widens with age.

Elevated A-a = intrinsic lung pathology (V/Q mismatch, shunt, diffusion impairment). Normal A-a with hypoxaemia = hypoventilation (lungs fine).

cards.front: EpiPen Jr (150 mcg) can be used from 7.5 kg; adult 300 mcg device from [___] kg; 500 mcg device from 50 kg.
cards.context: 150 mcg autoinjectors (EpiPen Jr, Anapen Jr) can be used in children over 7.5 kg. This is important for discharge planning and parent education.

cards.front: On VBG in sepsis, [___] is the key marker of tissue hypoperfusion that drives escalation of care.
cards.context: Systematic VBG interpretation: pH → CO₂ → HCO₃⁻ → lactate → electrolytes → haemoglobin. Lactate is a key marker of tissue perfusion in sepsis — raised lactate drives escalation of care.

cards.front: ANZCOR choking algorithm — severe obstruction (ineffective cough) while conscious: 5 back blows, then 5 chest [___]. If the patient becomes unresponsive, start CPR.
cards.context:
Choking management follows a stepwise algorithm based on severity assessment: effective cough (mild) vs ineffective cough (severe). Severe cases are further divided by conscious state.

Mild: encourage coughing. Severe + conscious: 5 back blows then 5 chest thrusts, repeat.

Severe + unconscious: finger sweep if visible, start CPR.

cards.front: Holliday-Segar sodium requirement for 70 kg: 2500 mL × [___] mmol per 100 mL = 75 mmol/day.
cards.context:
Holliday-Segar maintenance estimates daily Na need at ~3 mmol/100 mL (and K at ~2 mmol/100 mL).

Pure 0.9% saline (154 mmol Na/L) over-shoots adult Na requirements 5-fold — give it for resuscitation, not maintenance.

cards.front: Normal arterial base excess sits within ± [___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
VBG values are offset from ABG: pH ~0.03 lower, pCO₂ ~6 higher. HCO₃ and lactate are the same.

PaO₂ cannot be assessed on VBG.

cards.front: The default maintenance IV fluid for a euvolaemic patient with normal electrolytes is [___]% NaCl + 4% glucose.
cards.context:
The default maintenance fluid for a euvolaemic patient with normal electrolytes is 0.18% NaCl + 4% glucose. It provides 31 mmol/L Na+ (appropriate for maintenance needs) plus glucose to prevent ketosis.

0.9% NaCl and Hartmann's are resuscitation fluids with too much Na+ for maintenance.

cards.front: ATS Category 4 (potentially serious) has a maximum wait time of [___] minutes.
cards.context: ATS Category 4 covers conditions that may worsen if treatment is delayed beyond an hour but are unlikely to cause significant short-term harm — minor head injury without LOC, mild abdominal pain.

cards.front: VBG-to-ABG conversion offsets? pH: VBG [___] lower. pCO₂: VBG 3–8 mmHg higher. HCO₃⁻: Essentially same. Lactate: Same. PaO₂: Cannot assess from VBG.
cards.context:
VBG correlates well for pH, pCO₂, lactate, electrolytes. Main limitation: cannot assess PaO₂.

Use SpO₂ for oxygenation screening; ABG only when precise PaO₂/P:F ratio needed.
